answer_key: In (a) the segregated phase forms a continuous network running along the dendrite boundaries; in (b) it appears as isolated particles; in (c) it appears as thin, broken strings (o1). This progression shows that the rare-earth additions turn the coarse, continuous boundary phase into discontinuous, finer particles, with the effect stronger in the La-containing alloy than in the Sm-containing alloy (s1). Downstream, this refinement is linked to a tensile-strength ranking of Al-Cu-Mn-La > Al-Cu-Mn-Sm > Al-Cu-Mn (p3), attributed to La being more effective than Sm at breaking up the boundary phase, forming Al6Cu6La, and promoting dense fine theta' precipitates for higher strength (c1).
grading: Answer key: the labels and facts on the evidence node o1 (morphology/distribution across F1a-F1c), judge-confirmed against s1, p3 and c1 as the downstream chain the observation supports.
